title: Analytics Query Walkthrough
desc: Complete query demonstrating core ASQL syntax with detailed comments
query:
-- ASQL queries read top-to-bottom like a pipeline
-- Each line transforms the data from the previous step

from orders                          -- Start with a table (not SELECT)

  -- WHERE filters rows with conditions
  -- Use = for equality, standard operators work: <, >, <=, >=, !=
  where status = "completed"         
    and amount > 100                  -- AND combines conditions (both must be true)
    and customer_id is not null       -- NULL checking: IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
    and created_at >= @2024-01-01     -- @ prefix for date literals (cleaner than strings)
    and created_at < 30 days ago      -- Natural relative dates work too!

  -- GROUP BY with aggregates in parentheses
  group by region (
    sum_amount,                       -- Underscore shorthand: sum(amount) as sum_amount
    # as order_count,                 -- # is shorthand for COUNT(*)
    avg_amount,                       -- avg(amount) as avg_amount
    max_created_at as latest_order    -- Can override the auto-alias
  )

  order by -sum_amount                -- - prefix for descending (cleaner than DESC)
  limit 10                            -- Top 10 regions by revenue

title: Filtering Patterns
desc: Various WHERE clause patterns: strings, dates, NULLs, OR conditions
query:
-- This query demonstrates various filtering techniques

from users

  where status = "active"              -- Exact string match
    or status = "pending"              -- OR for alternatives
    
    and email is not null              -- NULL checking
    and email contains "@gmail.com"    -- String matching (preferred over LIKE '%...%')
    and name starts with "J"           -- Other string ops: ends with, contains
    
    and age between 18 and 65          -- BETWEEN for ranges
    and country in ("US", "UK", "CA")  -- IN for multiple values
    
    -- Date filtering options
    and created_at >= @2023-01-01      -- @ prefix for dates
    and last_login >= 7 days ago       -- Natural language dates
    
  select
    id,
    name,
    email,
    status,
    age,
    created_at
  order by created_at
  limit 100
